text:
noah: heads-up — several GPU pods pending in us-west1-b, CA isn't provisioning new nodes, looks quota-ish.

lucy: saw that, 14 pending gpu pods across ns=training and ns=jobs. GCE quota shows 0 spare A100s in us-west1-b.

noah: exact numbers from the dashboard: pending GPUs=14, needed nodes ~=6 (g4dn-style 4/gpu per node config).

hema: @noah can you paste the pod event? also which nodepool spec is requested (preemptible vs on-demand)?

noah: pasted events:
```
Normal Scheduled  Pod scheduled to default-scheduler
Warning FailedScheduling  2s (x50 over 5m)  cluster-autoscaler  did not find available capacity for this pod: 0/0 nodes are available: 6 Insufficient gpu.
```
nodepool label = gpu-training-pool, instanceType: a2-highgpu-1g (on-demand), taints: nvidia.com/gpu=true:NoSchedule

lucy: CA logs show it tried to create nodes in us-west1-b but GCE returned RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED for the zone. No fallback to other zones because the node template is zone-scoped and we pinned the pool to us-west1-b.

sre-oncall: deploy-bot reported a recent change to the regional allocation policy — PR #2387 restricted cross-zone auto-provisioning for that pool (safety lock).

noah: that PR was to reduce cross-zone noisy-neighboring, but now it's blocking any cross-zone failover in shortage scenarios. Not ideal.

hema: quick triage options: 1) temporarily relax the nodepool location constraint and let CA create in us-west1-c, 2) create a new regional nodepool (us-west1 region) with same labels/taints, 3) bump up on-demand quota request to GCP (long lead).

lucy: option 2 is safest short-term. Spin up a regional gpu pool with identical labels so schedulers can pick it up. Be careful: cost will increase if we don't use preemptibles.

noah: agreed. I'm +1 for regional pool but use preemptible where tolerable, and add a small on-demand reserved min (2 nodes) for critical jobs. Will also open a quota request to GCP for us-west1-b.

hema: run the commands I usually use to create the pool:
```bash
# create regional node pool (example gke)
gcloud container node-pools create gpu-regional-rt --cluster=prod-cluster --region=us-west1 \
  --machine-type=a2-highgpu-1g --num-nodes=0 --min-nodes=0 --max-nodes=20 \
  --node-taints=nvidia.com/gpu=true:NoSchedule --enable-autoscaling --labels=pool=gpu-training
```
And then set autoscaler policy to allow cross-zone placement.

lucy: also add this CA flag to allow balanced scale-ups across zones: `--balance-similar-node-groups` and ensure `--expander=random` isn't forcing single-group growth.

noah: note: some experiments (and PR #2387) were intentionally limiting cross-zone creation because of NVLink topology assumptions for certain model shards. We need to ensure workload affinity is respected — jobs that require co-located GPUs must still land in the same zone.

hema: for that, we can use podTopologySpread or nodeAffinity for jobs that require co-loc. For generic training jobs that tolerate distribution, use the regional pool. We'll tag nodepools with `topology=isolated` for zone-local workloads.

lucy: cost/ops note: regional preemptible nodes are cheaper but increase eviction churn. For long-running batches we should prefer on-demand reserved nodes. Budget impact estimate: ~+$6k/mo if we keep 2 on-demand A100-equivalents as min across region.

sre-oncall: I'll update the oncall runbook entry under ops/gpu-surge to include: 1) quick create regional pool snippet, 2) how to toggle policy in the allocation PR, 3) when to open quota requests. Link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-surge (needs a short add).

noah: action items:
- noah: create gpu-regional-rt pool as preemptible w/ min-nodes=0 max-nodes=20, mark with `pool=gpu-training` (ETA 15m).
- lucy: patch CA config to allow cross-zone creation for that pool and remove the safety lock in PR #2387 (ETA 1h).
- hema: open GCP quota ticket for us-west1-b A100s and request emergency soft increase (ETA <24h).
- sre-oncall: update runbook + postmortem template for zonal quota shortages (ETA end of day).

lucy: small follow-up: we'll also add a metric alarm on `gcp.gpu.quota.available` per zone so we get proactive alerts before pending pods spike.

deploy-bot: deploy status — gpu-regional-rt pool creation submitted (operation: op-1173), will post back when nodes are Ready. :rocket:

noah: testing scheduler behavior now — if any pending pods remain after pool Ready, we may need to relax pod anti-affinity on training jobs.

lucy: FYI I changed the CA setting to `balance-similar-node-groups=true` and allowed the regional pool to be used by autoscaler. Watch for unexpected pod redistribution.

deploy-bot: pool gpu-regional-rt nodes Ready (5 nodes preemptible) — scaling observed.

noah: confirmed 10 of 14 pending pods now scheduled. 4 remain because they requested full-node GPUs and prefer zone-local label `topology=isolated`.

hema: manual workaround: temporarily relax that affinity on non-critical jobs: `kubectl patch pod <pod> -p '{"spec":{"affinity":null}}'`. Do cautiously.

noah: logging this thread into the runbook, will include commands and the cost estimate. Thx all — follow-ups: PR to make cross-zone fallback opt-in via annotation instead of global lock.

lucy: noted, will draft the PR.

sre-oncall: closing loop: schedule a short retro with platform team tomorrow to discuss long-term: regional reservations, quota timeline, and a CA policy that supports controlled cross-zone failover. :white_check_mark:

noah: done — created ticket PLAT-4321 for the retro and linked this thread.
